subject.title: [Bug]: Mac app does not recover when installed bundle is replaced while running

question: Should OpenClaw.app automatically recover from an externally replaced installed bundle, or should supported update/deployment tooling be required to terminate the running app before replacement?
rationale: Both ownership boundaries are technically viable, but they establish different lifecycle and security contracts; the protected maintainer issue needs that contract chosen before implementation.

options.title: Add native self-recovery
options.body: Detect executable identity drift on activation or dashboard opening, validate the installed replacement, relaunch it once, and terminate the stale process.

options.title: Require coordinated replacement
options.body: Make updater and deployment paths terminate the running app before replacing the bundle, document external live replacement as unsupported, and provide a clear recovery prompt.

recommendation.title: Add native self-recovery
recommendation.body: Detect executable identity drift on activation or dashboard opening, validate the installed replacement, relaunch it once, and terminate the stale process.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is assigned to steipete and recent history shows broad ownership of the macOS app lifecycle and shell.
